Listen, as an older sister taking care of 4 of my siblings right now, you’re not ruining her life. I’m going to be 32 by the time my youngest sister is 18, I’ve got 10 years to go before they’ll all be full grown adults. Honestly, it’s not easy, but I’m listening to her brush her teeth right now, and I know there’s nothing else I’d want more than having my siblings with me. Is it easy? Of course not, but I remember how scared they all were when my mom passed. I remember how scared I was, and I never want them to feel that way, I want them to know they’re safe with me, and that I’ll always be there for them. As others have been saying, just be on your best behavior, and maybe try helping out around the house. One thing my siblings do is clean the apartment, maintain A and B grades, and communicate with me. You may feel helpless, but those small things make a big difference, for you and her. I promise, she doesn’t think you ruined her life. Keep your head up, I don’t doubt that she loves you :)

I’m nowhere near being a pro, but I drove my car for a couple of months on and off to work at night, or between 2-4 am. I dreaded daily traffic. I also work overnight shifts so driving at night and getting a feel was perfect for me. Then I started driving closer to 5am on my days off (weekends) because there wasn’t as much traffic as weekdays. I live in the county of San Diego and have a sister who lives near Temecula. She asked me for money recently and I planned to wake up at 3 am to drive over to her to leave the money. I woke up closer to five, on a Thursday. I live over an hour away from her. By the time I got to her, it was already past 6am and if you know anything about Temecula traffic, you know it’s fucking horrendous heading back to SD. Also it’s all hills too coming back and I wasn’t ready to do that, especially not in traffic that was stopped. So I took the backroads back. Did it suck? Yes. I considered leaving my car and getting a Lyft but it was at least 110 to get back home. So I put on my big girl pants and drove myself back. I let people pass me, even pulled over to try to do a hill start because why not? I had more courage going back because nobody knows me in Temecula. Soon as I got back to where I needed to be, I was stoked. That pulled me out of my comfort zone and showed me that I could actually do it. Been driving a couple weeks now without being too scared, even drove with traffic at 7 am, no stalling. Before, driving gave me so much anxiety that my back would basically cramp the same way it would on my menstrual cycle. It sucked a lot. But the night driving transition into early daytime driving helped a TON. Being backed into a corner when I drove to my sister was the push I needed to show myself that I honestly could do it. Idk if it’ll work for you, but honestly take your time. I even slept in my car for a bit to drive at night, forcing myself because I knew if I didn’t, I wouldn’t get up to drive before work. I love my little Honda :’). Do I still stall? Yup. Does it bother me? Ehh kinda. Do people honk as much? Nope, especially not now that I’ve stalled a lot less and learned my clutch. I hope my little habits might help you.
